subject: Political Science
chapter: Chapter 15: Recent Developments in Indian Politics
central_question: How did the major political developments since the late 1980s transform India's party system, social representation, debates on secularism and the emergence of a new political consensus?
in_scope_units: In this chapter and Context of the 1990s — the central questions and five developments that reshaped politics
Era of Coalitions — the 1989 election, National Front government and the beginning of coalition politics
Decline of Congress — the end of Congress dominance without an immediate single-party replacement
Alliance politics — multi-party competition, regional parties, United Front, BJP-led coalitions, NDA and UPA
Central Governments Since 1989 — the visual timeline of coalition and party-led governments
Political Rise of Other Backward Classes — OBC identity, political mobilisation and representation
'Mandal' implemented and The Mandal Commission — origins, recommendations, implementation, protests and the Indira Sawhney case
Political fallouts — BAMCEF, bahujan politics, Kanshi Ram and the rise of the BSP
Communalism, Secularism, Democracy — BJP, Hindutva, Shah Bano and politics based on religious identity
Ayodhya Issue and From Legal Proceedings to Amicable Acceptance — dispute, legal process and the Supreme Court verdict described in the chapter
Emergence of a new consensus — competition between Congress and BJP and the electoral charts
Lok Sabha Elections (2004-2019) — UPA, NDA, the 2014 and 2019 BJP majorities and continuing relevance of coalition politics
Growing consensus — four areas of broad agreement among political parties and continuing democratic contestation
Party Position in 17th Lok Sabha and Let Us Do It Together — visual and tabular electoral review
Exercises — chronology, matching, analytical questions and the Zoya Hasan passage
banned_topics: Detailed history of the Emergency and the pre-1980 party system beyond the brief background references made in this chapter
Detailed constitutional or electoral-system theory not used by the chapter to explain developments since the late 1980s
must_include_keywords: Political Rise of Other Backward Classes

known_pitfalls.claim: The defeat of Congress in 1989 meant Congress disappeared from national politics.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter says Congress lost its earlier centrality and dominance but remained an important party and returned to power after the 1991 elections.

known_pitfalls.claim: Coalition politics began because one new national party immediately replaced Congress.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter explains that Congress dominance declined without any single party immediately replacing it, leading to a multi-party era in which regional parties became crucial to ruling alliances.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Mandal Commission was only about political party alliances.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter says the Commission investigated educational and social backwardness, identified backward classes and recommended measures including reservation, which then had major political consequences.

known_pitfalls.claim: Dalit politics and OBC politics are presented as the same movement.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter says they often developed independently and sometimes in competition, even though bahujan politics sought to mobilise SC, ST, OBC and minorities together.

known_pitfalls.claim: The chapter presents the Ayodhya dispute as being resolved outside democratic and legal processes.
known_pitfalls.correction: The supplied text emphasises court hearings, mediation attempts, popular movements and the 2019 constitutional-bench verdict as part of due process of law and conflict resolution in a plural society.

known_pitfalls.claim: The emergence of a new consensus means political parties stopped competing.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter describes severe competition continuing alongside broad agreement on several major political and economic issues.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Exercise 3 to organise the major post-1989 issues and the party configurations they produced.
Use NCERT Exercise 4 to analyse why coalition alignments could cross ideological differences and focus on power-sharing arrangements.
Use NCERT Exercise 1 to build a source-grounded chronology linking Mandal, changing party formations, NDA, UPA and the Ram Janmabhoomi judgment.
Use NCERT Exercise 5 to trace the emergence of BJP through the chapter's discussion of post-Emergency reorganisation, Hindutva, Shah Bano, Ayodhya and later electoral growth.
Finish with NCERT Exercise 6 to assess how Congress continued to influence politics after losing its former dominance.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter's EXERCISES contain Questions 1-8, followed by a LET US DO IT TOGETHER activity and a party-position table for elections from 2004 to 2019.
